body:
@mihe: This is the best solution I came up with, maybe you see another?

An alternative would be to create a collector that records only the first hit per leaf shape but that would have the following problems:
* There would be no way to tell the collector to stop looking for hits in this particular leaf shape, so it would process all overlapping triangles of a ConcavePolygonShape3D where the current solution will stop after the first triangle that collides.
* There is no fast way to determine if a hit is for the same leaf shape. Since `SubShapeID` also encodes the triangle index, the only way you can know if a `SubShapeID` belongs to the same leaf shape is by calling `root_shape->GetLeafShape()` for every hit. This would mean traversing the shape hierarchy for every hit rather than once per leaf shape like we do now.

Another alternative would be to duplicate the code in `NarrowPhaseQuery::CollectTransformedShapes` and `Shape::CollectTransformedShapes` to record encountering JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape on the way down. This would be slightly faster/more robust, but duplicates a lot of code, so I didn't pick this solution.
Marking for cherry-picking for 4.7.3 to fix the regression there too, unless it's deemed a risky change and it's preferred to revert the cherry-pick of #120267 in `4.7` instead.

> maybe you see another?

If the issue with overriding `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape::CollectTransformedShapes` (as suggested in the MRP) is simply that we wrap the compound shape as a whole rather than the individual shapes, then what about doing something like this:

1. Combine `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` and `JoltCustomUserDataShape` into a single decorator, and call it something appropriately generic (`JoltCustomMetadataShape` or something?).
2. Pass double-sidedness down into `JoltShapeInstance3D::try_build`, and pass it along with the shape instance ID into something like a `JoltShape3D::with_metadata`.

I'm guessing that's probably a more pervasive change than what's proposed here, but it might at least save `intersect_shape` from becoming even messier.

What I'm not sure of right now is what that would mean for all the other (i.e. convex) shapes. We currently always wrap the concave shapes in `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` even when it's not technically double-sided, since Godot for whatever reason lets the shape dictate whether it can have its back-faces queried against.

EDIT: I'm realizing now that we also need to get `JoltConcavePolygonShape3D::back_face_collision` back up the chain to `JoltShapeInstance3D::try_build`. So I guess `JoltShape3D::_build` needs an out-parameter reporting whether the shape is double-sided or not.

> Combine JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape and JoltCustomUserDataShape into a single decorator

Not quite sure why this part is needed. The JoltCustomUserDataShape doesn't seem to cause any issues atm, so it doesn't matter where it is placed.

> I'm realizing now that we also need to get JoltConcavePolygonShape3D::back_face_collision back up the chain to JoltShapeInstance3D::try_build. So I guess JoltShape3D::_build needs an out-parameter reporting whether the shape is double-sided or not.

I guess this could work. As far as I can see, when a shape changes its double-sidedness it is destroyed and recreated. An area is always double sided, so I think you could combine these 2 bools into a single JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape just before the leaf shape. Maybe we should then only create JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape when the shape should be double sided. 

Note that this solution will stop to work if we ever decide that is is possible to have compounds of compounds (like https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/535 proposes - although the internal representation could still be a single compound for this proposal).

If you want me to change this, I can. Note that it could take a while before I get to it.

> Not quite sure why this part is needed. The JoltCustomUserDataShape doesn't seem to cause any issues atm, so it doesn't matter where it is placed.

Mostly to avoid the memory overhead/allocation of adding another decorator shape to every relevant shape instance. So instead piggybacking on the one per-instance decorator we already have.

Perhaps a bit overzealous in the grand scheme of things, but if the end result doesn't look too crazy, then I figured it might be justified.

> Maybe we should then only create JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape when the shape should be double sided.

If by "when the shape should be double sided" you mean when something like the `backface_collision` property on `ConcavePolygonShape3D` is enabled, then that might cause trouble, since ray-casts in Godot Physics behave in [this somewhat strange way](https://github.com/godot-jolt/godot-jolt/pull/551), meaning `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` serves just as much to stop the shape from being considered double-sided (in the context of ray-casts specifically) as it does to make it actually double-sided. It's a bit of a mess.

> Note that this solution will stop to work if we ever decide that is is possible to have compounds of compounds (like [godotengine/godot-proposals#535](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/535) proposes - although the internal representation could still be a single compound for this proposal).

I would indeed expect this to result in a single compound shape for the internal representation, and that is also how the pending pull request for it works as well: #77937

> If you want me to change this, I can. Note that it could take a while before I get to it.

I was actually chipping away at this yesterday, to see what it would look like, so I'll put up a PR within the next few days, assuming it actually works. I just need to test it a bit first.

The alternative approach is up now: #124080

I'll admit I'm not 100% sold on it. This new `JoltCustomInstanceOverridesShape` decorator isn't quite as intuitive as having `JoltCustomUserDataShape` and `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` separately, and the back-face stuff in `JoltCustomInstanceOverridesShape` ended up looking a bit weird with the two flags in there, but I struggle to see a better way to do it.
